items.title: Backup and disaster-recovery design
items.summary: Review A2 Administration-backed encrypted capture, deletion-aware exact retention, and isolated staged restore. Deleted source files remain protected for 30 days after verified deletion detection.
items.acceptance: Backup, restore, verification, exclusions, and secret handling have a reviewed reproducible procedure; retention preserves the last recoverable copy of a deleted path for 30 full days from verified deletion detection.
items.notes: A2 adds an Administration dropdown and Backup & Recovery page. It validates exact mount identity and source availability; keeps passwords page/operation-local; creates, checks, inventories, and receipts captures; integrates the A1 30-day deletion ledger; executes only exact hold-clear retention with dry-run, minimum/newest protection, bounded prune, and post-check; and restores only into verified owner-private staging. Deterministic verification passes. The hardened systemd deployment grants write access only to the configured recovery mount; live status reports the target ready and writable. Password-authenticated live capture/retention/restore remain human review actions.
items.implementation: BackupAdministrationService composes BoundedCommandRunner, restic, BackupRetentionLedger, SHA-256-bound previews, one nonblocking mutation lock, atomic owner-private manifests/receipts, and request-bound NDJSON progress. Restore terminates blocked_for_human_review and cannot promote staged data into live state.
items.technologies: Ruby, JavaScript, HTML/CSS, restic 0.19.1, ext4, JSON, SHA-256 digest binding, flock, owner-only atomic files, deterministic fixture verification.
items.interfaces: Dashboard: Administration → Backup & Recovery. Setup: Makefile preview/execute manifest configuration. Verification: Makefile target. No Chat invocation, scheduler, watcher, daemon, automatic retention, or live restore.
items.commands: make backup-config-plan; make backup-configure EXPECTED_DIGEST=... CONFIRM=CONFIGURE_SOUL_BACKUP_MANIFESTS; make verify-backup-administration.

items.source: Local Project and Document Search A2

items.title: Accepted stream disconnect completion
items.summary: A bounded operation already accepted by the Dashboard can reach its terminal lifecycle state after the client navigates away or disconnects during body delivery.
items.implementation: The original request thread stops writing to a disconnected socket but continues consuming the bounded response enumerator. Failure before headers still aborts immediately; no worker, queue, retry loop, or detached background process was added. Dashboard CSRF and static-route verification now checks behavior instead of stale exact counts.
items.technologies: Ruby HTTP server streaming lifecycle and deterministic verifier scripts.
items.interfaces: Dashboard streaming operations, including long-running Music and Visual generation requests.
items.acceptance: Body disconnects stop socket writes while accepted bounded work completes; header failures still abort before execution.

items.title: Push-to-talk, speech output, Voice Presence, and bounded perception foundations
items.summary: Local transcription, selectable speech, visible wake-word Presence, picture understanding, and explicit one-shot screen capture are implemented; newer follow-up behavior remains separately under live review.
items.implementation: Chat records one push-to-talk utterance, transcribes locally, and can submit it into the ordinary conversation runtime. Completed responses can be spoken with selectable voices. A visible PySide Voice Presence window performs bounded wake/listen/think/speak turns. Picture understanding accepts explicit attachments or fresh one-shot screen captures, preserves explicit monitor targets, withholds unsupported literal UI claims, and discards pixels by default.
items.technologies: Ruby conversation/perception services; Python 3.12 and PySide6 Presence app; whisper.cpp speech recognition; Supertonic 3 responsive CPU speech; optional Chatterbox expressive NVIDIA speech; RNNoise PipeWire virtual microphone; Gemma 4 multimodal analysis on Daily Core; Hyprland-aware capture helpers.
